newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: PRESS DIGEST - CENTRAL/EAST EUROPE - SEPT 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CENTRAL/EAST EUROPE - SEPT 18.

text.p: AUSTRIA
DER STANDARD
- Austria's inflation continues lower. In August inflation fell to 1.8 percent from 1.9 percent in July. The overall inflation rate for this year is expected to be 1.7 percent.
- German retailer Rewe is said to have taken over Austrian retailers Loewa and familia just months after having bought Austria's largest retailer Billa.
- Brickmaker Wienerberger is closing down two plants in the southern province of Styria due to the sluggish economy and expensive investments.
- Creditanstalt will open a branch in Singapore by the end of this year. It has also put in for a licence for a representative office in Beijing.
- Austria Faserwerke, currently owned by Lenzing, will be taken over by Germany's Hoechst in October.
DIE PRESSE
- Austrian petrol stations have raised prices for diesel and heating oil by 0.15 schillings due to higher international prices caused by the U.S.-Iraq conflict.
- 59 percent of Austrians agree that social cuts should be made to keep Austria more competitive. This is more than in any other country in the European Union.
- General Electric owns five percent of Austria's VA Technologie AG, the Vienna stock exchange announced.
KURIER
- Austria ranks third-last in an OECD ranking on revenue from privatisations.
- The consortium to buy the government's stake in Creditanstalt is not allowed to be changed, law specialists say following news that Die Erste savings bank might rejoin the consortium.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- European Union demands that sports goods maker Head-Tyrolia-Mares must either cut jobs or pay back a subsidy from the government.
ESTONIA
ALL NEWSPAPERS
- Siiri Oviir from the Centre Party and Tunne Kelam from the right-wing Pro Patria have agreed to stand at the presidential elections.

- Editor of a culture magazine, Juri Estam, and MPs Eldur Parder and Villu Muuripeal have turned to Tallinn City Court to argue their case that President Lennart Meri lied when he took his presidential oath.
POSTIMEES

- An interview with presidential candidate Tunne Kelam focusses on the forthcoming election. He said he is convinced he has a good chance to win the election and that Meri is the president for today while Estonia needs a president for tommorrow.
- A 200 hectare peat field is burning near the northeast Estonian town of Johvi, some 160 kms from Tallinn.
- The crew of the ferry Estonia are to receive offers of compensation this week, their lawyers said.
- An article highlights the alleged links of Lennart Meri with the KGB, allegations which have dogged the president for a long time.
SONUMILEHT
- The government has approved the 1997 draft budget of 22.8 billion kroons and a 1996 supplementary budget of 33 million kroons.
- The government has granted residence permits to 11,224 aliens, most of them Russian-speaking inhabitants. Three of them were dead when the document was issued.
- Justice Minister Paul Varul drove his car into a roadside post on Monday. The car, a government service vehicle, was damaged but the minister was unhurt.
EESTI PAEVALEHT

- The support group for the victims of the Estonia ferry disaster started a court case in France against the shipping yard that built the vessel, the Veritas certification bureau and the Swedish maritime department.
ARIPAEV
- The 1997 draft budget foresees three percent growth of gross domestic product (GDP) and 14 percent inflation.
CROATIA
VJESNIK
- Foreign Minister Mate Granic in Moscow: Russia interested in nurturing strong ties with Croatia.
- Bread and milk more expensive as of New Year!
- Croatia spends 88 million kuna per month on refugees.
VECERNJI LIST
- Counting of votes in Bosnia: Zubak, Izetbegovic and Krajisnik in the lead!
- Cost of living going up faster than wages. Industrial output in the first six months of 1996 4.3 percent in comparison to last year.
SLOBODNA DALMACIJA
- Is growth without inflation impossible?
- Confectioner Kras to follow in the footsteps of the Pliva farmaceuticals on the London bourse.
CZECH REPUBLIC

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Czech National Bank (CNB) put the largest fully-private Czech bank, Agrobanka, into temporary forced administration on Tuesday. President Vaclav Havel said he had full confidnce in CNB governer Josef Tosovsky's ability to handle the situation.

- Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus agreed with the leader of the opposition Milos Zeman (CSSD) that a parliamentary commission should be set up to look into the collapse of Kredtni Banka. The failure of Kreditni was partly responsible for the subsequent problems at Agrobanka.
- President Havel is in Brazil on the first leg of a 14 day official visait to South America.
- Motoinvest boss Pavel Tykac left the Czech Republic.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - Setuza said it would pay a dividend amounting to around 30 crowns per share on its 1995 profits.
PRAVO - The Communist party says it wil propose a vote of no confidence in the government.
LATVIA
ALL NEWSPAPERS

- Prime Minister Andris Shkele and leaders of the governing political parties signed an agreement on cooperation between the parties, aimed at stengthening the government and improving its work work. The pact takes the place of a formal coalition agreement although it has much the same effect.

- The board of the Democratic Party Saimnieks accepted the resignation of parliament speaker and leading member Ilga Kreituse. Kreituse said she was leaving because of the "dictatorship" of leader Ziedonis Chevers. Chevers has also initiated the dismissal of Finance Minister Aivar Kreituss.

- Latvian General Prosecutor Janis Skrastinsh met with Ilga Kreituse to discuss the possibility of bringing a criminal action against deputy Valdis Krisbergs, a member of the Democratic Party Saimnieks.
DIENA
- Latvian Christian Democrats Union deputy Maris Vitols and the working group including representatives from the Home Guard supported the introduction of military training at universities.

- Most of the governing factions believe that Minister of Finance Kreituss, expelled from his party, will stand down. They also say new candidates for the post will be proposed after the budget has been passed by parliament.
BIZNES I BALTIYA
- Two women stole $800,000 from Zemes Bank.
- A seminar on fighting money laundering will take place on September 20 with the participation of the U.S. embassy, the Association of Latvian Commercial Banks and the U.N. Drug Control Programme.

- The Ave Lat company, which controls some 60 percent of the stock exchange quoted Kaija fish cannery, is planning to issue new shares in Kaija although the size of the issue has not been decided yet.
NEATKARIGA RITA AVIZE
- The government has approved next year's budget draft, which has been drawn up without a deficit.
- The chancellor and deans of departments of the Latvian University are sceptical about the reforms of the univeristy proposed by state minister for higher education Peteris Cimdins.

- Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Stankevicius announced he is ready to meet Shkele at any time. He pointed out that Lithuania is waiting for Latvia's reply to proposals put forward at the last round of negotiations, a statement which surprised Latvian authorities, who have been looking forward to receive Lithuania's reply.
DIENAS BIZNESS

- A decision next week by European transport ministers could be important for Latvia as they set about approving the 10th multimodal corridor, which include Ventspils port as part of a corridor between western Europe and Russia. Latvia has so far been mentioned only in the corridor from Finland to Poland and western Europe along the Via Baltica.
